newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INSIGHT - HSBC seen resuming uptrend.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - HSBC seen resuming uptrend.

text.p: Feb 10 * Suprt * Rstnce * MA-50 * MA-200
HSBC Holdings Plc broke through resistance on Monday and could hit stride on another strong uptrend before the release of its 1996 earnings on March 3, analysts said.
"The share looks ready to form another uptrend...and to try to test another record high," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
The share broke through resistance at around HK$184.00 last week. On Monday, it set an all-time high of HK$191.50 in early trade before easing back to end HK$5.50 higher at HK$189.50.
The share leaped the equivalent of HK$5.00 in trade in London on Friday.
The London-listed share is trading at a three percent premium to the Hong Kong share, analysts said.
"This rally is really being led by London," said John Schofield, regional technical analyst at NAVA SC Securities.
HSBC is a constituent of both Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index and London's FTSE-100.
In Hong Kong, the share has advanced HK$24.00 or 15 percent since the start of the year.
The London-listed, sterling-denominated share has advanced 2.62 sterling or 20 percent as at Friday's close.
"The share had already given a reversal signal before the holiday break, showing a turnaround, that is a breakout from its HK$180.00 resistance level," said Shum.
The stock went through a consolidation during the second half of January. On February 5, the share advanced HK$2.00 to close at HK$184.00 in Hong Kong.
Short-term indicators look positive -- the 14-day relative strength indicator was advancing from the 74-point level and looked likely to test the 80-point level in the near term, analysts said.
"There is a very strong trend in place," said NAVA's Schofield.
While the indicators are trending into overbought territory, they have yet to make short-term peaks and could remain at the 80-point level for some time, said Schofield.
Analysts said Friday's breakout in London was due to the share's sensitivity to fluctuations in the U.S. dollar/sterling exchange rate.
The U.S. dollar has strengthened in recent days to a four-year high against the yen and was expected to be further boosted by favourable U.S. economic data released last Friday, analysts said.

Since the lion's share of the international banking giant's earnings are in U.S. dollars or dollar-related currencies, conversion of the bank's dollar earnings into sterling will -- on paper at any rate -- look even more bullish than the interim and quarterly earnings reports released so far.
"Fundamental factors, interest rates, currency and stock markets, are all bullish for the bank," said Schofield.
But technical analysts were reluctant to set a near-term or longer term upside for the share as it moves into uncharted territory.
